action.action-desc: Mr. Sanders introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

form.official-title: To provide additional funding for firefighter staffing and safety grants, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Firefighter Staffing and Support Act.
Section 33 of the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2229) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (d), by striking paragraph (4);
in subsection (q)(1)—

subparagraph.text: in the matter preceding subparagraph (A), by inserting , and there is appropriated, after appropriated;
in subparagraph (A), by striking and at the end;
in subparagraph (B)—

clause.text: in the matter preceding clause (i), by striking 2023 and inserting 2022; and
in clause (ii), by striking the period at the end and inserting a semicolon; and

subparagraph.text: by adding at the end the following:
$913,000,000 for fiscal year 2023; and
for each of fiscal years 2024 through 2028, an amount equal to the amount authorized for the previous fiscal year increased by the percentage by which—

clause.text: the Consumer Price Index (all items, United States city average) for the previous fiscal year, exceeds
the Consumer Price Index for the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year described in clause (i).

paragraph.text: by striking subsection (r).

section.text: The Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2201 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

In addition to amounts made available under sections 33(q)(2) and 34(j)(2), there is authorized to be appropriated, and there is appropriated, to provide technical assistance to qualified entities described in sections 33(c)(1) and 34(a) to prepare and submit an application for a grant under section 33(e) or 34(b)—

paragraph.text: $10,000,000 for fiscal year 2023; and
for each of fiscal years 2024 through 2028, an amount equal to the amount authorized for the previous fiscal year increased by the percentage by which—

subparagraph.text: the Consumer Price Index (all items, United States city average) for the previous fiscal year, exceeds
the Consumer Price Index for the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year described in clause (i).

section.header: Reports from FEMA and United States Fire Administration
section.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Administrator of the United States Fire Administration shall submit to Congress and make publicly available—

paragraph.text: a report on plans to improve the application process for grants under sections 33 and 34 of the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2229, 2229a) to ease access to those grant funds; and

a report on the challenges specific to rural and volunteer fire departments, as defined in section 33 of the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2229), which shall include an action plan to address these challenges through the grants described in paragraph (1) and other administrative action.

section.header: Protections for volunteers from employer discrimination
section.text: The Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 (15 U.S.C. 2201 et seq.), as amended by section 4 of this Act, is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Volunteer firefighter and EMS personnel job protection

paragraph.text: The terms emergency and major disaster have the meanings given those terms in section 102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5122).
The term qualified volunteer fire department has the meaning given such term in section 150(e) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.
The term volunteer emergency medical services means emergency medical services performed on a voluntary basis for a fire department or other emergency organization.
The term volunteer firefighter means an individual who is a member in good standing of a qualified volunteer fire department.

subsection.header: Termination of employment of volunteer firefighters and emergency medical personnel prohibited

paragraph.text: No employee may be terminated, demoted, or in any other manner discriminated against in the terms and conditions of employment because such employee is absent from or late to the employee's employment for the purpose of serving as a volunteer firefighter or providing volunteer emergency medical services as part of a response to an emergency or major disaster.
The prohibition in paragraph (1) shall apply to an employee serving as a volunteer firefighter or providing volunteer emergency medical services if such employee—

subparagraph.text: is specifically deployed to respond to the emergency or major disaster in accordance with a coordinated national deployment system such as the Emergency Management Assistance Compact or a pre-existing mutual aid agreement; or
is a volunteer firefighter who—

clause.text: is a member of a qualified volunteer fire department that is located in the State in which the emergency or major disaster occurred;
is a member of a qualified fire department that has a mutual aid agreement with a community affected by such emergency or major disaster; and
has been deployed by the emergency management agency of such State to respond to such emergency or major disaster.

paragraph.text: The prohibition in paragraph (1) shall not apply to an employee who—

subparagraph.text: is absent from the employee’s employment for the purpose described in paragraph (1) for more than 14 days per calendar year;
responds to the emergency or major disaster without being officially deployed as described in paragraph (2); or
fails to provide the written verification described in paragraph (5) within a reasonable period of time.

paragraph.text: An employer may reduce an employee’s regular pay for any time that the employee is absent from the employee's employment for the purpose described in paragraph (1).

An employer may require an employee to provide a written verification from the official of the Federal Emergency Management Agency supervising the Federal response to the emergency or major disaster or a local or State official managing the local or State response to the emergency or major disaster that states—

subparagraph.text: the employee responded to the emergency or major disaster in an official capacity; and
the schedule and dates of the employee's participation in such response.

paragraph.text: An employee who may be absent from or late to the employee’s employment for the purpose described in paragraph (1) shall—

subparagraph.text: make a reasonable effort to notify the employee’s employer of such absence; and
continue to provide reasonable notifications over the course of such absence.

paragraph.text: An individual who has been terminated, demoted, or in any other manner discriminated against in the terms and conditions of employment in violation of the prohibition described in subsection (b) may bring, in a district court of the United States of appropriate jurisdiction, a civil action against the employer of the individual seeking—

subparagraph.text: reinstatement of the individual’s former employment;
payment of back wages;
reinstatement of fringe benefits; and
if the employment granted seniority rights, reinstatement of seniority rights.

paragraph.text: The individual shall commence a civil action under this subsection not later than 1 year after the date of the violation of the prohibition described in subsection (b).

subsection.text: The Administrator of FEMA, in coordination with the Secretary of Labor, shall have the authority to issue rules to enforce this section.
